# cli-telemetry-spec

An honest usage signal for agent-first CLIs: one POST, one `telemetry` verb, one
allow-list of non-identifying fields, disclosed on stderr before anything is sent
and disabled by a single environment variable.

WHY: a CLI author cannot tell "nobody uses this" from "the install is broken".
Downloads, clones and stars all report the same zero. Agent-operated tools have
no human who will ever file an issue.

READ IN THIS ORDER
1. PROTOCOL.md      the normative contract (MUST/MUST NOT)
2. event.schema.json  the allow-list, machine-checkable (additionalProperties: false)
3. RECIPE.md        5 steps to implement it
4. SKILL.md         drop-in skill for adding it to a CLI

THE CONTRACT, COMPRESSED
- disclose on stderr before the first send; never on stdout
- honour <TOOL>_TELEMETRY=0 and DO_NOT_TRACK=1 BEFORE any network code runs
- automated fetch-and-run is NOT usage: audit tools, mirrors, scanners and image
  builds all look like a fresh install. Tools must honour DO_NOT_TRACK; harnesses
  that run other people's binaries must SET it. The reference implementation
  recorded 15 installs that were all its author's own install-checker.
- <TOOL>_TELEMETRY_URL is REQUIRED, not optional: without it the only way to see
  what a tool sends is to let it send
- default OFF in CI
- send only: tool, version, event(install|run|error), verb, os, arch,
  exit_class, optional random install_id, ts
- never send: hostname, username, paths, arguments, flag values, data, errors,
  env, or any machine-derived id
- never block, never retry, never change the exit code, never touch stdout
- `<tool> telemetry` prints the REAL next payload, produced by the send path
- collector aggregates; no IP logging, no profiles

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATION
grange (https://github.com/javimosch/grange) — `grange telemetry`

RELATED SPECS
cli-output-spec, cli-guide-spec, cli-feedback-spec, cli-update-spec
This is the fifth, and the only one that sends anything out. Adopt it last.
